candidates.excluded_reason: No independent test/result signal: neither phase runs a test suite or an independent evaluator — lab_books re-runs nine lab scripts, regenerate just confirms files are written. Smallest, but fails the selection criterion.

No dedicated test phase runs the tests it writes (reinterleave/endpoint add tests but nothing runs them as an independent gate), and its live side effects (SIGKILL worker.py PIDs, respawn workers on the live 6380 queue, verify-phase polling) confound the outcome with live-system state — a poor measurement cell.

candidates.notes: Dedicated 'test' phase runs `pytest tests/ -m "not external" -q` plus `kb_produce_registry.py --dry-run` — a deterministic, independent test_executed_success signal. Self-contained (dry-run only, no live queue mutation). NOTE: the p2 prompt listed this as workflows/repository/registry_canonicalize.yaml; the actual committed path is workflows/operations/registry_canonicalize.yaml (SHA256 recorded here is for the operations path).

candidates.excluded_reason: Not the smallest: 6 phases, ~7x the cost of registry_canonicalize.
Largest (7 phases, ~$1.45) and non-repeatable (repeatable: false, status completed).

selection.reason: The smallest candidate that both commits and has an independent test/result signal. labbook_refresh (cheapest) has no test signal; queue_steer (next cheapest) has no dedicated test phase and destructive live side effects. registry_canonicalize is self-contained, runs a real pytest gate as an independent signal, and is ~7x cheaper than the two closure specs.
